en: A fastening consisting of two metal rings, designed to go around a person's wrists, and connected by a chain or hinge.
Any abstract constraint, such as rules, regulations, or lack of resources.

handcuffs.ety:
1775, from hand + cuff (“end of shirtsleeve”).
Possibly influenced by Old English handcops, from hand + cops (“fetter, chains”), but due to lack of continuity (centuries between Old English and modern term), generally analyzed as a re-invention.

ex.en: I put handcuffs on him.
ex.ja: 私は彼に手錠をかけた。

note.ja: hand（手）+ cuffs（袖口）。「手錠」。

en: A religious recluse; someone who lives alone for religious reasons; an eremite.
A recluse; someone who lives alone and shuns human companionship.

hermit.ety: From Middle English hermite, heremite, eremite, from Old French eremite, from Ecclesiastical Latin, Late Latin eremita, from Ancient Greek ἐρημίτης (erēmítēs, “person of the desert”) from ἐρημία (erēmía, “desert, solitude”), from ἔρημος (érēmos) or ἐρῆμος (erêmos, “uninhabited”) plus -ίτης (-ítēs, “one connected to, a member of”). Doublet of eremite. Displaced native Old English ānsetla.

ex.en: The hermit lived in a wooden hut.
ex.ja: 隠者は木造の小屋に住んでいた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 erēmitēs（荒野に住む人）から。erēmos（さびしい・荒野）。「世捨て人」。hermit crab（ヤドカリ）。

en: To make difficult to accomplish; to act as an obstacle; to frustrate.
To delay or impede; to keep back, to prevent.
Of or belonging to that part or end which is in the rear or hind, or which follows.

hinder.ety: From Middle English hindren, from Old English hindrian, from Proto-Germanic *hindrōną, *hinderōną (“to hinder”), from Proto-Germanic *hinder (“back”) (adverb). Cognate with Dutch hinderen and German hindern, Latin contra (“back, against”).

ex.en: He didn't come to help, but to hinder us.
ex.ja: 彼は助けに来たというより邪魔しに来た。

ex.en: She didn't come to help, but to hinder us.
ex.ja: 彼女は我々の手伝いに来たというより、邪魔しに来たようなものだ。

ex.en: She hindered me in my study.
ex.ja: 彼女が私の勉強を妨げた。

note.ja: 古英語 hindrian（妨げる）から。behind と同系。「後ろへ引き止める」→「妨げる」。

ex.ja: 君には病気の時助けてもらった恩義がある。

en: Offensive to good taste.
Not in keeping with conventional moral values; improper, immodest, or unseemly.

ex.en: He has given us indecent wages.
ex.ja: 彼はわたしらに少ない賃金しかくれなかった。

ex.en: He reformed his indecent ways.
ex.ja: 彼は淫らな生活から足を洗った。

note.ja: in（否定）+ decent（きちんとした）。「下品な」。

An inquiry, typically into an undesired outcome

inquest.ety: From Middle English enquest, from Old French enqueste (Modern French enquête), from Vulgar Latin inquirere, or from Medieval Latin inquesta < in + Latin quaesita.

en: The sound of metal or glass clattering against itself.
A small piece of metal attached to a musical instrument, such as a tambourine, so as to make a jangling sound when the instrument is played.
To make a noise of metal or glass clattering against itself.
To cause to make a noise of metal or glass clattering against itself.

jingle.ety: The verb, which is older than the noun, is from Middle English gyngle. Onomatopoeic; compare jangle.

note.ja: 擬音語。「チリンチリン」→ 耳に残る短い曲 →「CMソング」。

en: To laugh loudly.
To gasp for breath as in a severe fit of coughing.
A tight curl, twist, or bend in a length of rope, line, or other long cylindrical material, such as hair etc.
A cramp or stiffness in a part of the nody, especially the neck or back.

kink.ety: From Middle English kinken, kynken, from Old English *cincian (attested in cincung), from Proto-West Germanic *kinkōn, from Proto-Germanic *kinkōną (“to laugh”), from Proto-Indo-European *gang- (“to mock, jeer, deride”), related to Old English canc (“jeering, scorn, derision”). Cognate with Dutch kinken (“to kink, cough”).

en: A large and heavy motor vehicle designed to carry goods or soldiers; a truck
A truck with an open carriage, sometimes used for transporting construction workers.
To transport by, or as if by, lorry.

lorry.ety: Uncertain; perhaps from dialectal English lurry (“to lug or pull about, drag”) (compare dialectal lurry-cart), or from the forename Laurie. First attested in early to middle 19th century.

ex.en: I was almost hit by a lorry.
ex.ja: もう少しでトラックにはねられるところだった。

ex.en: In Britain a truck is referred to as a lorry.
ex.ja: イギリスではトラックはローリーと呼ばれる。

ex.en: The lorry had to stop because its load had fallen off.
ex.ja: 積み荷が落ちたので、トラックは停車しなければならなかった。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。lurry（引く）とされる。（英）「トラック」。

en: A tree or shrub in any species of the genus Magnolia, many with large flowers and simple leaves.
The flower of a magnolia tree.
Of a creamy white colour, like that of some magnolia flowers.

magnolia.ety:
Borrowed from translingual Magnolia, from French Magnol + -ia. Named after French botanist Pierre Magnol (1638–1715). The surname is a form of the male given name Magne, from Latin magnus, which in turn from Proto-Italic *magnos, from Proto-Indo-European *m̥ǵh₂nós, from *méǵh₂s (“great”).
.

note.ja: 17世紀のフランスの植物学者マニョル（Pierre Magnol）の名前から。

en: Migrating.
Roving; wandering; nomadic.

migratory.ety: Borrowed from Latin migrātōrius or migrate + -ory.

ex.en: Many migratory birds come to this pond every year in winter.
ex.ja: この池には、毎年冬になるとたくさんの渡り鳥がやってきます。

en: To intermix; to combine or join, as an individual or part, with other parts, but commonly so as to be distinguishable in the product.
To associate or unite in a figurative way, or by ties of relationship.
The act of informally meeting numerous people in a group.

mingle.ety: From earlier mingil, mengle, from Middle English menglen, equivalent to ming + -le. Cognate with Dutch mengelen (“to mingle, mix”), German mengen (“to mingle, mix”). More at ming.

ex.en: She had never mingled in the society of women.
ex.ja: 彼女は一度も女の社会で交際したことがなかった。

ex.en: The colors don't mingle well.
ex.ja: 色がうまく調合しない。

ex.en: He had a look that mingled fright with surprise.
ex.ja: 彼は恐怖と驚きの混ざった表情をしていた。

en: A set of rules used for forming the names or terms in a particular field of arts or sciences.
A set of names or terms.

nomenclature.ety: Borrowed from Latin nōmenclātūra (“a calling by name, list of names”), from nōmen (“name”) + calāre (“call”). Doublet of nomenklatura.

note.ja: ラテン語 nomenclatura（名前を呼ぶこと）から。nomen（名前）+ calare（呼ぶ）。「命名法」。

A strong protest.

To cry louder than.

From Middle English outcry, outcri, outcrye, equivalent to out- + cry.

ex.en: The outcries of the angels go unheard by ordinary human ears.
ex.ja: 普通の人間は天使の叫びが聞こえない。

note.ja: out（外へ）+ cry（叫び）。「抗議の叫び」。

To cover with stone, concrete, blacktop or other solid covering, especially to aid travel.

note.ja: play（劇）+ house。「劇場」。

note.ja: preference（好み）+ -tial。「優先的な」。

To lengthen in time; to extend the duration of.

prolong.ety: Either a back-formation from prolongation, or from Old French prolonguer or porloignier, from Latin prōlongō, from prō + longō. Doublet of purloin.

ex.en: I'd like to prolong my stay in America.
ex.ja: 私はアメリカ滞在の期間を延長したい。

ex.en: Gooseberries can prolong your life.
ex.ja: スグリは長寿に有効な果物だ。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ longus（長い）。「長引かせる」。prolonged と同じ。

propane.ety: From clipping of propionic acid + -ane, from French propionique, from Ancient Greek πρό (pró) + πίων (píōn, “fat”). Analyzable as prop- + -ane, borrowing or calque of German Propan.

ex.en: Propane is a gas.

note.ja: propionic acid（プロピオン酸）+ -ane。ギリシャ語 pro（前の）+ piōn（脂肪）。

To instruct to go, inquire, elsewhere.
A redirection.
An examination of a witness, following cross-examination, by the party that conducted the direct examination, re-examination.

tramp.ety:
From Middle English trampen (“to walk heavily”), from Middle Low German trampen (“to stamp”) (trampeln (“to walk with heavy steps”), see trample) or from Middle Dutch trampen (“to stamp”), from Proto-West Germanic *trampan (“to step”). Doublet of tremp.
Cognate with Dutch trampen (“to stamp, kick, step”), dialectal German trampen (“to step, walk, tread”), whence commoner German trampeln (“to trample”). Probably related to trap.

ex.en: I can't bear to tramp ten miles in this heat.
ex.ja: この暑さに１０マイルもてくてく歩くのはたまらない。

ex.en: Don't tramp in the living room with muddy feet.
ex.ja: 泥だらけの足で居間をどたどたあるいてはいけない。

ex.en: Stray dogs tramped about my garden.
ex.ja: 野犬がうちの庭を踏み荒した。

note.ja: 中英語 trampen（踏みつける）から。「どしどし歩く」→ 歩き回る人 →「浮浪者」。trample と同じ。

en: A solid-state semiconductor device, with three terminals, which can be used for amplification, switching, voltage stabilization, signal m…

transistor.ety: Blend of transfer + resistor. Said to have been coined by American engineer John Robinson Pierce in 1947, who used transresistance as the basis for forming transistor.

ex.en: The invention of the transistor introduced a new era.
ex.ja: トランジスタの発明で新しい時代が始まった。

ex.en: The invention of the transistor marked a new era.
ex.ja: トランジスターの発明は新時代を画した。

note.ja: transfer（伝達）+ resistor（抵抗器）を合わせた語。1948年の造語。

en: A gait of a person or animal faster than a walk but slower than a run.
A brisk journey or progression.
To move along briskly; specifically, to move at a pace between a walk and a run.
To move at a gait between a walk and a canter.

trot.ety: From Middle English trotten, from Old French trotter, troter (“to go, trot”), from Medieval Latin *trottō, *trotō (“to go”), from Frankish *trottōn (“to go, run”), from Proto-Germanic *trudōną, *trudaną, *tradjaną (“to go, step, tread”), from Proto-Indo-European *dreh₂- (“to run, escape”). Cognate with Old High German trottōn (“to run”), Modern German trotten (“to trot, plod”), Gothic 𐍄𐍂𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (trudan, “to tread”), Old Norse troða (“to walk, tread”), Old English tredan (“to step, tread”). Doublet of trade and tread.

ex.en: The boy trotted to his father's side.
ex.ja: その男の子は父親のそばへちょこちょこ走って行った。

ex.en: He walked quickly away with two dogs trotting at his heels.
ex.ja: 早足でついていく２匹の犬をすぐ後に従えて、彼は急いで歩き去った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 troter（速足で歩く）から。「速足」。

en: The highest point, top or apex of something.
The highest surface on the skull; the crown of the head.

vertex.ety: Late Middle English, borrowed from Latin vertex (“whirl, eddy; top, crown, peak, summit”). Doublet of vortex.

ex.en: How many vertices and faces does a pentagonal prism have?
ex.ja: 五角柱の頂点の数と面の数は，それぞれいくつですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 vertex（渦・頂点）から。vertere（回す）。「頂点」。vortex と同系。

en: Something made from wood, especially cabinets and trim (e.g., baseboards, doorframes) made from millwork.
Working with wood.

woodwork.ety: From Middle English woodewerk (“carpentry”), equivalent to wood + work.

ex.en: Their highest skill was woodworking.
ex.ja: 彼らの最高の技術は木工細工に見られた。

ex.en: In woodworking, we classify wood as hardwood, softwood or exotic wood.
ex.ja: 木工芸では、木を、硬木、軟木と、唐木に分類します。

note.ja: wood（木）+ work（細工）。「木工・木工品」→ 木管楽器（woodwind）とは別。

en: The quality or state of being acid.
Sourness; tartness; sharpness to the taste.

acidity.ety: From French acidité, from Latin aciditātem, accusative singular of aciditās (“sourness, acidity”), from acidus (“sour, acid”). Equivalent to acid + -ity.

ex.en: Coffee without acidity seems to suit my father's taste better.
ex.ja: コーヒーは酸味のないものの方が父の嗜好に合うようだ。

note.ja: acid（酸）+ -ity。ラテン語 acidus（酸っぱい）。「酸性度・酸味」。

en: Again, once more; afresh, in a new way, newly.

anew.ety: From Middle English onew, of newe, from Old English of niowe. By surface analysis, a- (“of, from”) + new.

ex.en: I will begin anew.
ex.ja: 新たに始める。

note.ja: a（〜で）+ new。「新たに」。

en: To make quiet; to calm; to reduce (something) to a state of peace; to dispel (anger, hatred, etc.).
To make conciliatory offerings or concessions to (someone) in an attempt to dispel their anger, aggression, etc.; to adapt to the demands…

appease.ety: From Middle English apesen, from Old French apeser (“to pacify, bring to peace”).

ex.en: Management tried to appease labor by offering them a bonus.
ex.ja: 経営者側は労働者側にボーナスを出すと言って譲歩しようとした。

ex.en: Only a sincere apology will appease my anger.
ex.ja: 私の怒りを静めるのは心からの謝罪しかない。

ex.en: Her kindness appeased his anger.
ex.ja: 彼女のやさしさが彼の怒りをしずめた。

en: A natural ability to acquire knowledge or skill.
The condition of being suitable.

aptitude.ety: From Middle French aptitude, from Medieval Latin aptitudo, from Latin aptus (“apt, fit”). By surface analysis, apt + -itude. Doublet of attitude.

ex.en: He has an aptitude for painting.
ex.ja: 彼は絵の才能がある。

ex.en: He has a remarkable aptitude for music.
ex.ja: 彼は音楽の素晴らしい才能をもっている。

ex.en: Genius is nothing but a great aptitude for patience.
ex.ja: 天才とは忍耐に堪え得る偉大な適性に外ならぬ。

note.ja: ラテン語 aptitudo（適性）から。aptus（ふさわしい）。「適性・才能」。apt と同じ。

en: The back side of anything, the part opposite its front, particularly
The back side of an estate: the backyard and outbuildings behind a main house, especially (UK dialect, euphemistic) an outhouse.
Approaching an obstacle backward.

ex.en: Those who are cute have a hateful backside.
ex.ja: 憎い憎いは可愛いの裏。

note.ja: back（後ろ）+ side（側）。「裏側」→「お尻」。

Relating to someone who makes custom-made products, especially clothing items.

bespoke.ety: In sense “custom-made”, 1755, from earlier bespoken (c. 1600), form of bespeak, in sense “arrange beforehand” (1580s), a prefixed variant of speak; compare order, made-to-order.

note.ja: bespeak（前もって注文する）の過去分詞。「注文された」→「あつらえの」。

A sudden release of oil and gas from a well.

en: Full of liveliness and activity; characterized by quickness of motion or action.
Full of spirit of life; effervescing.
To make or become lively; to enliven; to animate.

brisk.ety: Uncertain; probably a collateral form of brusque, but compare Irish briosc, Scottish Gaelic brisg, Welsh brys.

ex.en: Industrial activity is brisk.
ex.ja: 産業界が活気づいています。

ex.en: Sales are amazingly brisk.
ex.ja: 売れ行きはものすごく活発だ。

ex.en: It's invigorating to breathe the brisk, fresh mountain air.
ex.ja: 山でおいしい空気をすうと気分も爽快です。

note.ja: フランス語 brusque（ぶっきらぼうな）から変化したとされる。「きびきびした」。

en: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis, an annual variety of cabbage, of which the cluster of young flower stalks and buds is eaten as a vegetable.
The edible head or curd of a cauliflower plant.
To (cause to) swell up like a cauliflower ear.

cauliflower.ety: From 16th century cole-florye, equivalent to cole (from Latin caulis) + flower, reformed to more closely match the Latin etymon. By surface analysis, caul(is) + -i- + flower. Cognate with French chou-fleur, Italian cavolfiore.

ex.en: I like broccoli, but I hate cauliflower.
ex.ja: ブロッコリーは好きですが、カリフラワーは大嫌いです。

ex.en: Cauliflower and broccoli are similar.
ex.ja: カリフラワーとブロッコリーは似てます。

note.ja: イタリア語 cavolfiore ＝ cavolo（キャベツ）+ fiore（花）。「花キャベツ」。kale と同じ。

en: A power saw that has a power-driven and fast-revolving chain of metal teeth, usually used to cut trees.
To cut with a chainsaw.
To make quick and substantial spending cuts.

chainsaw.ety: Compound of chain + saw in reference to the chain-cutting mechanism.

ex.en: Why do you need a chainsaw?
ex.ja: なんでチェーンソーが必要なの？

note.ja: chain（鎖）+ saw（のこぎり）。「チェーンソー」。

en: A distinctive member (Acinonyx jubatus) of the cat family, slightly smaller than the leopard, but with proportionately longer limbs and a…

cheetah.ety: Borrowed from Hindi चीता (cītā, “leopard, panther”), ultimately from Sanskrit चित्र (citra, “multicolored, speckled”) (akin to Old High German haitar (“bright”) > German heiter; Old Norse heiðr (“bright”)) + Sanskrit काय (kāya, “body”), thus “having a spotted body”.

ex.en: A cheetah runs as fast as any animal.
ex.ja: チータは他のどの動物にも劣らず速く走る。

ex.en: The cheetah is the fastest animal.
ex.ja: 一番速い動物はチーターです。

ex.en: Cheetahs cannot climb trees.
ex.ja: チーターは木には登れないんだ。

note.ja: ヒンディー語 cītā（まだらの）から。サンスクリット語 citra（まだらの）。

ex.ja: 彼は複雑なぜんまいじかけのおもちゃを考案した。

en: The state of things being similar or identical.
A point of resemblance; a similarity.

conformity.ety: From Middle English conformyte, from Middle French conformité. By surface analysis, conform + -ity.

ex.en: Conformity is an essential element of our homogeneous community.
ex.ja: 同じような人々からなる私たちの地域社会では、体裁に従おうとする意識は不可欠な要素である。

note.ja: con（共に）+ form（形）+ ity。形を同じにすること →「順応・一致」。conform（従う）。

en: The spouse of a monarch.
A husband, wife, companion or partner.
of a title, by virtue of one's (living) spouse; often contrasted with regnant and dowager
To associate or keep company (with).
To be in agreement.

consort.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, ultimately from Latin cōnsors. As “companion or partner”, via Middle English consorte.

note.ja: ラテン語 consors（運命を共にする人）から。con + sors（運命）。「配偶者・交際する」。consortium と同じ。

en: To compare things and bring them into a relation having corresponding characteristics.
To be related by a correlation; to be correlated.
Either of a pair of things related by a correlation; a correlative.
Showing regard or thought for others; especially, displaying good manners or etiquette.

courteous.ety:
From Middle English curteis, from Old French curteis (French courtois), from cort (“court”). By surface analysis, court + -eous.
Compare typologically Czech zdvořilý (<~ dvůr), German höflich (<~ Hof). Also note Russian прийти́сь ко двору́ (prijtísʹ ko dvorú).
Compare typologically civil, urbane. See pagan for the opposite.

ex.en: You must be courteous to any guest.
ex.ja: あなたはどんなお客にも礼儀を尽くさねばならない。

ex.en: It is very courteous of you to call on me.
ex.ja: 訪ねてきてくださって本当にありがとうございます。

ex.en: It was courteous of him to write a letter of thanks.
ex.ja: 礼状を書くとは彼も礼儀正しかった。

note.ja: courtesy（礼儀）と同じ。古フランス語 corteis（宮廷風の）。court（宮廷）+ -eous。「礼儀正しい」。

en: In a curious manner; with curiosity; inquisitively.
Oddly; in a strange or unexpected way.

curiously.ety: From Middle English curiusly, curyously, curiosly, curiouseliche, curyouslyche, equivalent to curious + -ly.

ex.en: The townspeople looked curiously at me.
ex.ja: 町の人達は物珍しそうに私を見た。

ex.en: Curiously, a flower bloomed on the withered up tree.
ex.ja: 奇妙なことに枯れた木に花が咲いた。

note.ja: curious（好奇心の強い・奇妙な）+ -ly。「物珍しそうに・奇妙なことに」。

en: To delay or postpone.
to postpone induction into military service.

defer.ety: Originally a variant of (and hence a doublet of) differ; from Middle English differren (“to postpone”), from Old French differer, from Latin differō. Doublet of differ and dilate. See also infer, collate and confer, delate and defer, relate and refer as well as prelate and prefer among others.

ex.en: I defer to your judgement.
ex.ja: 私は君の判断を尊重する。

note.ja: ラテン語 differre（先へ運ぶ）から。「延期する」→ 判断を相手に任せる →「従う（defer to）」。differ と同じ語源。

A transformation to eliminate intermediate data structures within a program.

en: The social, non-verbal behaviors (such as body language and facial expressions) that are characteristic of a person.

demeanor.ety: From Middle English demenure, from the verb Middle English demenen, demeinen (“to handle, manage”), from Old French demener (“to guide, conduct”), from de- + mener (“to conduct, lead”), from Latin *mināre (“to drive”) and minor (“to project or jut forth”).

ex.en: The teacher had a cold demeanor.
ex.ja: 先生は冷ややかだった。

ex.en: She has a graceful demeanor.
ex.ja: 彼女の物腰はしとやかだ。

ex.en: From beginning to end Tom has only spoken with a lackluster demeanour.
ex.ja: トムは最初から最後まで淡々と話した。

note.ja: demean（ふるまう）+ -or。古フランス語 demener（導く）。「態度・物腰」。

en: To be felt sorrow for; worthy of compassion; lamentable.
Deserving strong condemnation; shockingly bad, wretched.
A person or thing that is to be deplored.

deplorable.ety:
The adjective is borrowed from French déplorable (“lamentable, regrettable”), or from its etymon Late Latin dēplōrābilis + English -able (suffix meaning ‘relevant to, suitable to’). Dēplōrābilis is derived from Latin dēplōrō (“to bemoan, complain about; to bewail, lament, deplore”) + -ābilis (suffix meaning ‘able or worthy to be’); while dēplōrō is from dē- (intensifying prefix) + plōrō (“to cry out; to complain; to lament, deplore”) (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₃(w)- (“to flow; to swim”)). By surface analysis, deplore + -able.
The noun is derived from the adjective. Noun sense 2 re

ex.en: It is deplorable that she is so selfish.
ex.ja: 彼女がこれほど自分勝手なのは嘆かわしい。

note.ja: deplore（嘆く）+ -able。de + plorare（泣く）。「嘆かわしい」。explore と同じ plor。

en: Any non-soap cleaning agent, especially a synthetic surfactant.
Synonym of cleansing.

ex.ja: 心の痛みを感じたおまえを追うのが怖かった。

A grotesque misrepresentation.

To represent someone in an exaggerated or distorted manner.

A pack of cigarettes, usually ten, wrapped in cellophane or packed in a light cardboard box.
To put in a carton.

en: A branched, often ornate, light fixture suspended from a ceiling.

ex.ja: ガラス製のシャンデリアがテーブルの真上に下がっていた。

ex.en: There was a beautiful chandelier hanging from the ceiling.
ex.ja: 天井から美しいシャンデリアが下がっていた。

note.ja: フランス語 chandelier（ろうそく立て）から。chandelle（ろうそく）。candle と同じ語源。

A solidified mass of any liquid.

ex.ja: 心配すんな。血はすぐ止まるよ。

note.ja: 古英語 clott（塊）から。cloud、clod と同系。「（血の）塊」。

The state of being a journeyman.

ex.ja: 誰か女性の相手が欲しかった。

en: Uncritically satisfied with oneself or one's achievements; smug.
Unduly unworried or apathetic with regard to a need or problem.

complacent.ety: Borrowed from Latin complacēns (“very pleasing”), present participle of complacēre (“to please at the same time, be very pleasing”), from com- (“together”) + placēre (“to please”); see please and compare complaisant.

en: To press, force, or drive, particularly in filling, or in thrusting one thing into another; to stuff; to fill to superfluity.

ex.ja: 塾の先生と付き合っている。

ex.ja: その少年は衣類を残らず鞄に詰め込んだ。

craven.ety: From Middle English cravant, either borrowed from Old French cravanté (“defeated”), past participle of cravanter (ultimately from Latin crepare), or a modification of creaunt (“defeated”) after craven (“to crave”).

en: A particular period of history, or of a person's life, especially one considered noteworthy or remarkable.
A notable event which marks the beginning of such a period.
To divide (data) into segments by time period.

epoch.ety: From Medieval Latin epocha, from Ancient Greek ἐποχή (epokhḗ, “a check, cessation, stop, pause, epoch of a star, i.e., the point at which it seems to halt after reaching the highest, and generally the place of a star; hence, a historical epoch”), from ἐπέχω (epékhō, “to hold in, check”), from ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + ἔχω (ékhō, “to have, hold”). ex.ja: この見地から歴史は２つの主要な時期に分けられる。

ex.en: There have always been fashionable faces and expressions which marked an epoch.
ex.ja: ある時代の特徴となる流行の顔と表情というものが、常に存在した。

exaggerate.ety: Borrowed from Latin exaggerātus, perfect passive participle of exaggerō (“to heap up, increase, enlarge, magnify, amplify, exaggerate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from ex- (“out, up”) + aggerō, aggerāre (“to heap up”), from agger (“a pile, heap, mound, dike, mole, pier, etc.”), from aggerō, aggerere (“to bear, carry to (some place), bring together”), from ad- (“to, toward”) + gerō (“to carry”).

ex.ja: 誇張はやめなさいって100万回言ったでしょ。

ex.ja: 教育の重要性はいくら強調してもしすぎることはない。

ex.en: I think that Tom is exaggerating.
ex.ja: トムは大げさに言ってるんだと思う。

en: Having been quenched or eliminated.

ex.en: The fire was extinguished at once.
ex.ja: 火事はただちに消された。

ex.en: The fire was soon extinguished.
ex.ja: その火事はすぐに鎮火された。

ex.en: My hope has been extinguished by his remark.
ex.ja: 彼の発言で私の希望は失われた。

Confused, befuddled, or vague.

foggy.ety: From fog + -y, originally in the sense "covered with tall grass; marshy; thick". ex.ja: 外は霧がかかっている。

ex.ja: 彼女はゆっくりと霧のかかった森の中へ消えていった。
